claims.text: Adding a small amount of oxygen or nitrogen interstitials to a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature mechanical capability.
The interstitial modification will limit the alloy's density increase.
The interstitial modification will preserve room-temperature performance.
The proposed benefit should hold above 1000 K under high-stress loading.
Oxygen or nitrogen interstitials will form ordered interstitial complexes in the refractory high-entropy alloy.
Oxygen or nitrogen interstitials will produce solid-solution strengthening.
Ordered interstitial complexes impede dislocation motion.
Ordered interstitial complexes enhance strain hardening.
Impeded dislocation motion and enhanced strain hardening will improve high-temperature mechanical capability.
Relative to an interstitial-free as-cast or wrought refractory high-entropy alloy, the modified alloy will have increased yield strength.
Relative to an interstitial-free as-cast or wrought refractory high-entropy alloy, the modified alloy will have increased elongation.
There is an upper interstitial-content threshold beyond which the alloy's microstructure and properties will be negatively affected.
The ordered-interstitial-complex mechanism is supported by PMC7304825 and PMC7513042.
